title: Add DIS radio stream analysis support
description: This MR adds DIS stream analysis across both tshark and the Qt UI. On the CLI side, it introduces -z dis,streams to summarize DIS radio/audio streams with timing, jitter, loss, and problem indicators. On the GUI side, it adds DIS Streams and DIS Stream Analysis dialogs with stream discovery, per-packet metrics, waveform visualization, and audio playback controls including progress and play/pause behavior. Regression coverage includes a DIS sample capture test and a DIS fuzz target.

Tried this on my Windows setup with the sample capture provided in the test folder.  When I clicked on Play, I get "Audio format is not supported by the current output device." - Do I need additional libraries, etc?
Also, when I click the Analyze button, Wireshark crashes (looks like due to lack of parent widget)

Thanks! I'm now working in both mac and windows machines to better cover issues. Both issues are fixed in the latest update. The playback path now adapts the decoded DIS audio to the device’s preferred Qt output format on Windows, and the Analyze action now opens the dialog with a valid QWidget parent instead of crashing.
Rather than be a global (that needs to be "reset" for each packet), you can allocate this structure with pinfo->pool scope when passing it into tap_queue_packet()
Good catch. I changed the DIS tap info from a global to a per-packet allocation in pinfo-\>pool and pass that through tap_queue_packet(), so there’s no global packet state to reset anymore.

+#
+# Wireshark tests - DIS dissection tests
+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+#
+'''DIS (Distributed Interactive Simulation) dissection tests'''
+
+import subprocess
+
+DIS_DECODE_AS_ARGS = ('-d', 'udp.port==6993,dis')
+
+
+class TestDissectDis:
+    '''Tests for DIS dissection and stream analysis tap.'''
+
+    def test_dis_protocol_present(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''Verify the sample capture is dissected as DIS.'''
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark,) + DIS_DECODE_AS_ARGS + (
+                '-r', capture_file('dis_voice_sample.pcap'),
+                '-Tfields',
+                '-eframe.protocols',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+        lines = [line for line in stdout.strip().split('\n') if line]
+        assert lines
+        assert any(':dis' in line or line.endswith('dis') for line in lines)
+
+    def test_dis_streams_stat_output(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''Verify the DIS streams tap reports the expected stream summary.'''
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark,) + DIS_DECODE_AS_ARGS + (
+                '-r', capture_file('dis_voice_sample.pcap'),
+                '-q',
+                '-z', 'dis,streams',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+        assert 'DIS Streams' in stdout
+        assert '172.17.34.253' in stdout
+        assert '255.255.255.255' in stdout
+        assert '0x0002' in stdout
+
+    def test_dis_packet_count(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''Verify packet parsing does not crash on the DIS capture.'''
+        proc = subprocess.run((cmd_tshark,) + DIS_DECODE_AS_ARGS + (
+                '-r', capture_file('dis_voice_sample.pcap'),
+                '-q',
+            ), capture_output=True, text=True, env=test_env)
+        assert proc.returncode == 0, f"tshark failed: {proc.stderr}"
